title: 2 Samuel Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 4.

questions.question: What happened to Saul's son when he heard that Abner was dead in Hebron?
questions.correctAnswer: His hands were feeble
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:1 states that when Saul's son heard that Abner was dead, his hands were feeble.

questions.question: Who were the two captains of bands under Saul's son?
questions.correctAnswer: Baanah and Rechab
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:2 tells us that Saul's son had two captains named Baanah and Rechab.

questions.question: From which place were Baanah and Rechab, the sons of Rimmon?
questions.correctAnswer: Beeroth
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:2 identifies Baanah and Rechab as sons of Rimmon a Beerothite.

questions.question: Where did the Beerothites flee and become sojourners?
questions.correctAnswer: Gittaim
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:3 states that the Beerothites fled to Gittaim and were sojourners there.

questions.question: Who was lame of his feet and five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan?
questions.correctAnswer: Mephibosheth
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:4 identifies Mephibosheth as the lame son of Jonathan, Saul's son.

questions.question: How did Mephibosheth become lame?
options: He fell while his nurse fled
He was struck by a beast
questions.correctAnswer: He fell while his nurse fled
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:4 explains that Mephibosheth became lame because he fell as his nurse fled.

questions.question: At what time of day did Rechab and Baanah come to Ishbosheth's house?
options: At the heat of the day
questions.correctAnswer: At the heat of the day
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:5 says they came about the heat of the day to Ishbosheth's house.

questions.question: What did Rechab and Baanah pretend to be doing when they came into Ishbosheth's house?
questions.correctAnswer: Fetching wheat
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:6 states they came as though to fetch wheat.

questions.question: What did Rechab and Baanah do to Ishbosheth?
options: They smote, slew, and beheaded him
questions.correctAnswer: They smote, slew, and beheaded him
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:7 describes that they smote, slew, and beheaded Ishbosheth.

questions.question: Where did Rechab and Baanah take Ishbosheth's head?
questions.correctAnswer: To David in Hebron
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:8 says they brought the head to David in Hebron.

questions.question: What was David's response to Rechab and Baanah after they brought Ishbosheth's head?
questions.correctAnswer: He condemned and executed them
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:11-12 shows David condemned them and had them killed.

questions.question: True or False: Mephibosheth was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:4 states Mephibosheth was five years old at that time.

questions.question: True or False: Rechab and Baanah were sons of Saul.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:2 states they were sons of Rimmon, a Beerothite, not sons of Saul.

questions.question: True or False: David killed the man who first told him that Saul was dead.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:10 says David killed the man who brought him the news of Saul's death.

questions.question: True or False: David rewarded Rechab and Baanah for killing Ishbosheth.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:11-12 shows David punished Rechab and Baanah by killing them and hanging their limbs.

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What happened to Ishbosheth when Rechab and Baanah came to his house at noon?
options: They smote him under the fifth rib and killed him
questions.correctAnswer: They smote him under the fifth rib and killed him
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:5-6 describes how Rechab and Baanah came to Ishbosheth's house and smote him under the fifth rib, killing him.

questions.question: How did Rechab and Baanah approach Ishbosheth’s house according to 2 Samuel 4:6?
options: They came openly with their weapons
They disguised themselves as wheat harvesters
They came as though to fetch wheat
They entered through the back door
questions.correctAnswer: They came as though to fetch wheat
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states that they came into the house as though they would have fetched wheat before attacking Ishbosheth.

questions.question: What did Rechab and Baanah do with Ishbosheth's body after killing him?
options: They left the body in the house
They beheaded him and took his head away through the plain all night
They took him to Hebron alive
questions.correctAnswer: They beheaded him and took his head away through the plain all night
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:7 explains that after killing Ishbosheth, they beheaded him and carried his head away through the plain during the night.

questions.question: What reason did Rechab and Baanah give David for killing Ishbosheth?
options: To gain favor with Saul's family
Because Ishbosheth was David's enemy who sought his life
Because they wanted to take over the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: Because Ishbosheth was David's enemy who sought his life
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:8 records that they told David Ishbosheth was his enemy who sought to take David's life, and that the LORD had avenged David.

questions.question: How did David respond to Rechab and Baanah after they presented the head of Ishbosheth to him?
options: He condemned and executed them for killing a righteous man in his own house
He sent them away with a warning
questions.correctAnswer: He condemned and executed them for killing a righteous man in his own house
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:9-11 shows David condemning their deed because Ishbosheth was killed wickedly in his own house and then commanding their execution.

questions.question: What punishment did David command for Rechab and Baanah after their crime?
options: They were slain, their hands and feet cut off, and hung over the pool in Hebron
questions.correctAnswer: They were slain, their hands and feet cut off, and hung over the pool in Hebron
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:12 records David commanding his young men to kill them, cut off their hands and feet, and hang them over the pool in Hebron.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 4:11 imply about David’s view of justice and murder?
options: David accepts murder if done for political gain
David demands that bloodshed must be punished, especially murder in one’s own house
David ignores crimes against his enemies
David rewards those who kill his enemies
questions.correctAnswer: David demands that bloodshed must be punished, especially murder in one’s own house
questions.explanation: Verse 11 shows David asserting that he must require their blood because they wickedly killed a righteous person in his own bed.

questions.question: What does the passage in 2 Samuel 4 teach about integrity and leadership?
options: Leaders should reward all who bring them advantage
Leaders must uphold justice even against those who seek to serve them
Leaders should ignore crimes if politically convenient
Leaders should accept gifts from anyone
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders must uphold justice even against those who seek to serve them
questions.explanation: David’s refusal to reward murderers and his execution of them (4:9-12) highlight the importance of justice and integrity in leadership.

questions.question: True or False: Ishbosheth was killed while he was awake and preparing for battle.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:5-7 states Ishbosheth was lying on his bed at noon in his bedchamber when he was killed, indicating he was not preparing for battle.

questions.question: True or False: Rechab and Baanah fled immediately after killing Ishbosheth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:6 mentions that after they smote Ishbosheth, Rechab and Baanah escaped immediately.

questions.question: What lesson about trust in God’s justice can we draw from David’s reaction to the murder of Ishbosheth?
options: David trusts God to reward evil deeds
David takes justice into his own hands by killing the murderers
David trusts God’s justice and punishes wickedness to uphold righteousness
David ignores the murder because it benefits him
questions.correctAnswer: David trusts God’s justice and punishes wickedness to uphold righteousness
questions.explanation: David acknowledges God’s redemption (4:9) and punishes the murderers to uphold justice (4:11-12), showing trust in divine justice.

questions.question: How does the narrative in 2 Samuel 4 demonstrate the biblical virtue of humility in leadership?
options: David humbles himself by refusing to accept a violent act as a gift
David humbles himself by hiding from enemies
David humbles himself by seeking revenge on all his enemies
David shows humility by accepting all gifts
questions.correctAnswer: David humbles himself by refusing to accept a violent act as a gift
questions.explanation: David’s refusal to accept the murder of Ishbosheth as a favor (4:9-10) shows humility and respect for God’s justice.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 4:12 teach about the consequences of wrongdoing even if done in the name of loyalty?
options: Wrongdoing is always overlooked if done for loyalty
Wrongdoing will be punished regardless of claimed loyalty
questions.correctAnswer: Wrongdoing will be punished regardless of claimed loyalty
questions.explanation: David orders the execution of Rechab and Baanah despite their claim of serving him, showing wrongdoing is punished irrespective of loyalty (4:12).

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 4:10 reveal about David's attitude toward receiving news of Saul's death?
options: He rewarded the man who told him
He killed the man who falsely brought him news expecting a reward
questions.correctAnswer: He killed the man who falsely brought him news expecting a reward
questions.explanation: Verse 10 states David killed the man who brought news of Saul's death, because he expected a reward, showing David’s rejection of deceitful motives.

questions.question: True or False: David buried the head of Ishbosheth in the sepulchre of Abner after the execution of the murderers.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:12 states that after executing the murderers, they took Ishbosheth’s head and buried it in Abner’s sepulchre in Hebron.

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 4.

questions.question: To whom did Rechab and Baanah bring the head of Ishbosheth?
questions.correctAnswer: David
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:8 states that Rechab and Baanah brought the head of Ishbosheth to David in Hebron.

questions.question: What reason did Rechab and Baanah give David for killing Ishbosheth?
options: He was a traitor to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He sought David's life
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 4:8, they say Ishbosheth sought David's life, and that the LORD had avenged David of Saul and his seed.

questions.question: What was David's initial reaction to the killing of Ishbosheth by Rechab and Baanah?
options: He condemned them and ordered their execution
questions.correctAnswer: He condemned them and ordered their execution
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:11-12 shows David condemning their action as wicked and commanding his men to kill them and hang their hands and feet over the pool in Hebron.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 4:10, where did David kill the man who brought him news of Saul's death?
questions.correctAnswer: Ziklag
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:10 states that David killed the man in Ziklag who brought news of Saul's death, thinking to reward him.

questions.question: What was the fate of Rechab and Baanah after David condemned them?
options: They were slain and their hands and feet cut off
They fled to a foreign land
questions.correctAnswer: They were slain and their hands and feet cut off
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:12 describes how David's young men killed them, cut off their hands and feet, and hung them over the pool in Hebron.

questions.question: Who was Mephibosheth, mentioned in this chapter?
options: Jonathan's son who was lame of his feet
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan's son who was lame of his feet
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:4 identifies Mephibosheth as Jonathan's son who became lame after falling while fleeing.

questions.question: What was the original meaning of the name 'Beerothite' linked to the sons of Rimmon?
questions.correctAnswer: Man of wells
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root 'beer' means 'well,' so 'Beerothite' refers to 'man of wells,' consistent with Rimmon the Beerothite's origin in 2 Samuel 4:2.

questions.question: Which city became the place of refuge for the Beerothites after fleeing, according to this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Gittaim
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:3 states that the Beerothites fled to Gittaim and were sojourners there.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in David's speech condemning Rechab and Baanah, especially in contrasting the killing of Saul's servant and Ishbosheth?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:9-11 uses parallelism by contrasting the killing of Saul's servant (considered iniquitous) with the killing of a righteous man in his own house, emphasizing justice.

questions.question: True or False: David accepted the killing of Ishbosheth as a divinely sanctioned act and rewarded Rechab and Baanah.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:11-12 shows David condemning the murder and executing Rechab and Baanah, indicating he did not approve or reward their act.

questions.question: Which earlier biblical event is echoed by David's statement 'As the LORD liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity'?
options: Job's declaration of faith in Job 13:15
questions.correctAnswer: Job's declaration of faith in Job 13:15
questions.explanation: David's phrase in 2 Samuel 4:9 parallels Job 13:15's expression of trusting God's redemption through adversity.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of God avenging the death of the righteous as seen in David’s response to Ishbosheth’s murder?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 12:19
questions.explanation: Romans 12:19 speaks of leaving vengeance to God, paralleling David’s insistence on divine justice for Ishbosheth’s murder in 2 Samuel 4:11.

questions.question: True or False: The burial place of Ishbosheth's head was the same as Abner's sepulchre in Hebron.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:12 states that Ishbosheth's head was buried in the sepulchre of Abner in Hebron.

questions.question: Which theme from 2 Samuel 4 is foreshadowed by the violent death of Ishbosheth and the political instability that follows?
options: The eventual unification of Israel under David
The exile of the Israelites to Babylon
The division of the kingdom under Solomon
questions.correctAnswer: The eventual unification of Israel under David
questions.explanation: The death of Ishbosheth (2 Samuel 4:6-7) removes a rival to David, foreshadowing Israel's unification under David’s rule as narrated later in 2 Samuel.

questions.question: What cultural practice does David's punishment of Rechab and Baanah reflect about ancient Near Eastern justice?
options: Public execution and display of criminals to deter others
questions.correctAnswer: Public execution and display of criminals to deter others
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:12 describes the cutting off of hands and feet and hanging over a pool, which reflects public display as a deterrent common in ancient Near Eastern justice.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Saul's son's reaction to Abner's death in Hebron reveal about his state and the reaction of Israel?
options: His hands were feeble and all Israel was troubled
He celebrated Abner's death and Israel was joyful
He was indifferent and Israel was confused
He sought vengeance immediately and Israel was divided
questions.correctAnswer: His hands were feeble and all Israel was troubled
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:1 states that when Saul's son heard of Abner's death, his hands were feeble and all Israel was troubled, indicating fear and instability among Saul’s followers.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 4:2, what is significant about the lineage of Baanah and Rechab?
options: They were sons of Rimmon, a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: They were sons of Rimmon, a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:2 identifies Baanah and Rechab as sons of Rimmon, a Beerothite, from the tribe of Benjamin, highlighting the tribal affiliations important in Israel's sociopolitical landscape.

questions.question: What theological implication can be drawn from the account of Mephibosheth's lameness as narrated in 2 Samuel 4:4?
options: It shows human frailty and the consequences of fleeing in fear
It was a divine punishment for Saul’s family
It symbolizes the spiritual weakness of Israel
It indicates Mephibosheth's unfitness for kingship
questions.correctAnswer: It shows human frailty and the consequences of fleeing in fear
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:4 reveals Mephibosheth's lameness resulted from his nurse's haste to flee after Saul and Jonathan's death, illustrating human vulnerability and the tragic results of fear.

questions.question: What does the method of Ishbosheth’s murder by Rechab and Baanah in 2 Samuel 4:5-7 suggest about the nature of sin and violence in the narrative?
options: It reflects the treachery and calculated brutality in the struggle for power
It was an act of justified war against a tyrant
It symbolizes divine judgment executed by God’s agents
It was an accidental killing during a wheat gathering
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the treachery and calculated brutality in the struggle for power
questions.explanation: Verses 5-7 describe a deliberate, deceitful assassination of Ishbosheth in his bedchamber, highlighting human sinfulness, violence, and ambition contrary to God's justice.

questions.question: How does David’s response to the murderers of Ishbosheth in 2 Samuel 4:8-11 reveal his understanding of justice and kingship?
options: He condemns their act and demands retributive justice
He rewards them for removing an enemy
He ignores their deed to maintain peace
He negotiates a political alliance with them
questions.correctAnswer: He condemns their act and demands retributive justice
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:8-11 shows David rejecting the murderers’ claim of loyalty, emphasizing that killing a righteous man in his own house is wrong, thereby upholding divine justice and the sanctity of life under his kingship.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated through God's vindication of David in the punishment of Ishbosheth’s murderers (2 Samuel 4:11-12)?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: David’s ordering of the execution and public humiliation of the murderers in 2 Samuel 4:11-12 manifests God's attribute of justice, showing that wickedness against the righteous will be punished.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 4:3's note on the Beerothites' exile to Gittaim contribute to our understanding of covenantal and tribal dynamics in Israel?
options: It shows the consequences of tribal displacement and the fragility of tribal identity
It indicates divine exile as a punishment for sin
It reflects a voluntary migration for economic reasons
It demonstrates God’s promise to preserve the tribe
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the consequences of tribal displacement and the fragility of tribal identity
questions.explanation: Verse 3 explains the Beerothites fled to Gittaim and remained sojourners, reflecting how political turmoil led to tribal displacement, affecting Israel’s covenantal tribal structure.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching regarding the sanctity of life and retributive justice can be synthesized from 2 Samuel 4:6 and 2 Samuel 4:11?
options: Human life is sacred and unlawful killing demands punishment
Violence is acceptable to gain political advantage
Retribution is personal and private, not state-sanctioned
Justice is flexible according to the king’s discretion
questions.correctAnswer: Human life is sacred and unlawful killing demands punishment
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:6 recounts the unlawful murder of Ishbosheth, and 4:11 shows David’s insistence on punishing the murderers, teaching the doctrine that human life is sacred and killing the righteous is punishable by law.

questions.question: How does the burial of Ishbosheth’s head in the sepulchre of Abner (2 Samuel 4:12) reflect theological themes of honor and reconciliation?
options: It signifies posthumous honor and an attempt to reconcile fractured leadership
It is a sign of disrespect to his family
It indicates David’s rejection of Ishbosheth completely
It shows neglect of proper burial customs
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies posthumous honor and an attempt to reconcile fractured leadership
questions.explanation: Verse 12 records the burial of Ishbosheth's head in Abner's sepulchre, symbolizing respect and a theological hope for unity and peace despite political violence.

questions.question: What overarching narrative arc does 2 Samuel 4 contribute to in the biblical story of redemption?
options: The consolidation of David’s kingdom as a precursor to the Messianic lineage
The rejection of monarchy as a divine institution
The rise of Saul’s dynasty to eternal glory
questions.correctAnswer: The consolidation of David’s kingdom as a precursor to the Messianic lineage
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4, through the death of Ishbosheth and David’s just actions, advances the narrative of God establishing David’s legitimate rule, which foreshadows the Messianic kingdom (2 Samuel 4:8-12; 2 Samuel 4:1).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that David’s execution of Ishbosheth’s murderers was politically motivated and unjust. What does 2 Samuel 4:9-12 actually teach about David’s understanding of justice?
options: David upholds divine justice by condemning murder regardless of political benefit
David rewards political allies regardless of morality
David ignores justice to secure his reign
David acts out of personal vengeance
questions.correctAnswer: David upholds divine justice by condemning murder regardless of political benefit
questions.explanation: Verses 9-12 show David condemns the murder of a righteous man and enforces capital punishment on the murderers, emphasizing justice over political expediency, reflecting God’s holiness (2 Samuel 4:9-12; Proverbs 21:15).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is reflected in the narrative of the slain Ishbosheth as David’s response reveals God's moral order?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: David’s condemnation of the murder in Ishbosheth’s house highlights God’s holiness, which demands purity and justice, not tolerating the shedding of innocent blood (2 Samuel 4:10-11; Habakkuk 1:13).

questions.question: What combined theological insight about human sin and divine justice emerges from 2 Samuel 4:5-7 and 2 Samuel 4:11?
options: Sinful treachery leads to divine retribution enforced through human justice
Violence is a divine mandate in times of political strife
God tolerates human sin for the sake of peace
Justice is irrelevant in the context of royal succession
questions.correctAnswer: Sinful treachery leads to divine retribution enforced through human justice
questions.explanation: The brutal murder in verses 5-7 and David’s condemnation and punishment in verse 11 together teach that human sinfulness provokes divine justice, which is administered through human authority in line with God’s moral law.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God’s providence can be gleaned from the effect of Abner’s death on the political situation in 2 Samuel 4:1 and the subsequent events?
options: God sovereignly directs history to fulfill His redemptive plan
God is passive in human political affairs
Human history is chaotic without divine order
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly directs history to fulfill His redemptive plan
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 4:1 shows the destabilization after Abner’s death, yet David’s rise and the unfolding events demonstrate God’s providential control over history to bring about His purposes (Romans 8:28; Psalm 75:6-7).

questions.question: How do the actions of Baanah and Rechab in this chapter illustrate the biblical doctrine of human depravity?
options: Their deceitful and violent murder of Ishbosheth shows the pervasive corruption of sin in humanity
Their loyalty to David shows human goodness
Their flight from Gittaim shows fear of God
Their respect for tribal laws shows moral integrity
questions.correctAnswer: Their deceitful and violent murder of Ishbosheth shows the pervasive corruption of sin in humanity
questions.explanation: The chapter’s account of Baanah and Rechab’s treacherous killing (2 Samuel 4:5-7) demonstrates human sinfulness and depravity, consistent with biblical teaching that all humans are fallen and inclined to evil (Romans 3:10-12).
